dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 2.5-hour, flat-bottomed dip repeating every 13.1 days on a nearby M dwarf with depth about 0.4%. No nearby star within one pixel can mimic it, there is no odd-even or secondary eclipse, and the duration matches the star's size for a ~3 Earth-radius planet. The depth looks very different between the TESS pipelines and between individual transits, but this is expected for a bright-spot, rapidly rotating cool star with sparse data, and alone does not favour a binary.

reasons.why: No star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can produce the 4266 ppm dip with <=25% eclipse; closest plausible at 26.9 arcsec needs 5.6% and is far outside one pixel. Low contamination and no Gaia binarity flags argue the dip is on the target, with no positive evidence for a neighbour EB.

Flat-bottomed, central-duration transit implies a planet-sized companion (2.9 Rearth with TIC radius 0.4126, 3.36 Rearth with Gaia FLAME 0.470) on a short-period M dwarf, positively favouring transit over stellar EB.
